shape_construction: Believable task-specific proportions, silhouettes, construction, joins and object anatomy. Generic boxes, disconnected pipes, floating parts and unclosed architectural gaps are substantive defects. Judge intended stylization, not polygon count.
materials: Appropriate authored material vocabulary, scale, surface differentiation and consistency. Default/checker surfaces, indiscriminate tiling and texture pasted over primitive geometry do not establish finish. Do not demand wear where not requested.
lighting: Exposure, readable surfaces, shadow depth, light/material relationships across all important zones. Burnt-out whites, persistent darkness, flat unreadable surfaces and pervasive glare lower quality even if objects exist.
composition: Spatial hierarchy, focal readability, coherent massing and purposeful distribution at overview, street/room and close scales. Empty space is not inherently bad; unjustified barren requested working or inhabited zones are.
detail: Meaningful task-specific equipment, furnishing and environmental detail at large/medium/small scales. Repeated colored boxes, labels and token props cannot stand in for differentiated functional objects or rich requested spaces.
style: Match the requested/reference visual language across all zones. Real environments require plausible construction and material treatment; voxel/game styles require intentional resolved abstraction. Do not penalize coherent low-poly/voxel design for not being photorealistic.
scene_coverage: Substantive realization of the public brief and reference scene extent, connected zones, context and principal architectural/environmental features. Judge the realized scene, not merely presence counts or labels. Avoid requiring identical camera or incidental photograph clutter.
functional_identity: Visible differentiation and credible furnishing of required functional areas and mechanisms. A named room with token objects is partial credit. Compare defining reference features when supplied. Do not infer actual interactive success from appearance.

formula: continuous quality anchored to visible completion; coverage and deviation retained separately as diagnostics

environment.criterion: The tall central keep dominates a connected complex of lower buildings, enclosed courtyards and stone-supported terraces.
Preserve the pronounced elevation changes: broad exterior stairs rise between buildings, while overlapping roofs occupy multiple heights below the keep.
Exterior spaces have closely spaced architectural edges, substantial retaining walls and narrow gaps, conveying a dense fortified compound.
Include both the exterior courtyard approach and the principal interior gallery setting, with coherent floor heights and architectural scale.
Exterior atmosphere is wintry and subdued, with a gray lavender sky, distant haze, falling snow and uneven snow deposits on roofs and ground.
Maintain the contrast between cold, diffuse exterior light and dim timber interiors punctuated by small warm hanging lanterns.

features.criterion: A tall, tapering stack of roofed stories rises above a much wider lower mass.
Broad projecting roofs have lifted corners, overlapping triangular gables and a prominent curved central gable profile.
Facade bays are divided by substantial timber posts and horizontal beams, with recessed panels and closely spaced vertical window slats.
Roof edges show repeated rounded tile ends, layered ridge caps and restrained ornamental crest details.
Dark weathered brown timber, muted plaster panels and charcoal gray tiles establish the keep's aged exterior palette.
Tall battered stone bases support the buildings and define steep-sided courtyard approaches.
A long, broad straight stair climbs toward a recessed entrance between elevated structures.
Retaining walls use irregular, visibly jointed stone blocks with coarse surfaces and varied sizes.
Snow collects along stair edges and ground margins while darker central tread surfaces remain visible.

targets.label: Stone foundations and connected courtyard approach

features.criterion: Lower gatehouses, projecting bays and side towers form an uneven stepped roofscape around the keep.
The courtyard-facing gatehouse has a prominent triangular gable above wide eaves and a lower tiled roof.
Deep eaves expose repeated supporting members; timber posts frame pale wall panels and dark rectangular openings.
Gray ceramic roof tiles form continuous parallel courses, with cylindrical caps along ridges and decorative gable crests.
Weathered wood and stained beige plaster match the keep, with light snow emphasizing roof courses.
A broad upper gallery wraps around a large rectangular opening to the floor below.
Heavy square posts and multiple horizontal timber rails enclose the opening, with substantial corner posts.
Wall elevations are organized into repeated timber-framed bays, with lower screen panels and upper pale panels or dark slatted sections.
Broad wooden floorboards show strong grain, uneven coloration and worn reflective patches.
Dark structural wood contrasts with subdued cream and ochre screens bearing landscape and tree paintings.

targets.label: Interior timber gallery and screen-lined rooms

features.criterion: Small hanging lanterns sit high along the interior perimeter and emit localized warm yellow light.
Visible exterior fittings include a simple wooden rack against a plaster wall and barrels near the stair entrance.
Sparse winter vegetation occupies snowy margins beside the approach rather than obscuring the architecture.
